newsitem.title: USA: Spot heat oil off amid talk of big NYMEX delivery.
newsitem.headline: Spot heat oil off amid talk of big NYMEX delivery.

text.p: Eroding middle distillate prices were all the rage in U.S. spot oil markets Tuesday amid talk one player had taken a voluminous delivery of NYMEX-grade heating oil, traders said.

Prompt 86-grade wet material changed hands at 1.90 cents over the March print -- more than 0.50 cent weaker than diffs on Monday. Including the sharp NYMEX losses, that meant heat prices have slipped nearly 2.00 cents a gallon in a day.
The talk of heating oil deliveries on the now-expired February contract centered on midcontinent producer/refiner Koch Oil. Koch was not immediately available to comment.

The NYMEX meanwhile said PaineWebber Inc accepted a total 2,159 lots, or 2.2 million barrels, with traders in futures and cash markets pointing to Koch as the main player for whom PaineWebber had cleared those barrels.
In U.S. Gulf markets, distillate diffs were heading the other way, with barrels of prompt 74-grade low sulphur diesel heard done at 0.25 cent over March NYMEX heating oil.
While some players acknowledged Koch may be up to some sophisticated trading strategy, they also said it may be simply a bullish gamble with the weather that has failed.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1633
